data.narrative:
Senra Systems, a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jordan Black and Ben Shanahan, has raised $112M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of 3 private companies at identical stage and sector (Robotics & Manufacturing), supplemented by a broader universe of 8 private comparables and 1 public reference point.

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression analysis uses the $112M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $213M. Peer-median analysis examines three same-sector, same-stage comparables—Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B)—producing a median valuation of $1.8B and a range of $1.6B to $2.0B. The peer-median method carries greater weight given direct comparability on stage and sector.

The analysis supports a range of $181M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $981M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around whether Senra's operational metrics and market traction align with the lower end of the peer distribution or toward the median. Critical variables include revenue growth trajectory, customer concentration, and capital efficiency relative to the peer cohort. Narrowing this range requires additional diligence on unit economics and near-term revenue visibility.
